html:
The Treaty of Bardo was signed on 12 May 1881 at the Bardo palace near Tunis, after French troops had crossed the border from Algeria. The bey of Tunis accepted French control of his foreign affairs and army, making Tunisia a French protectorate.

Tunisia was bankrupt, its finances run by a commission of its European creditors since 1869. France, Italy and Britain all wanted influence there. France used raids by tribesmen across the Algerian border as its pretext.

The bey stayed on his throne, but French officials ran the country, and French and Italian settlers took much of the best land. Resistance grew into the nationalist movement of the Destour and later Bourguiba's Neo-Destour. France ended the protectorate in 1956.
